features.logic_and_math: Each stem processed by Humanize with seed = 1000 + hash(stem_name) so vocal and drum wow/flutter don't move in lockstep. A stem with Custom groove enabled passes its own wow_rate_hz/depth_ms/level_var_db/noise_floor_db to that stem's _apply_humanize call; a stem without it falls back to the shared global scalar. Sum peak-normalized to -0.3 dBFS to prevent clipping. Non-destructive; result loaded as the loudness-matched A/B B (fires X-Ray + What Changed).
features.why_it_exists: Different instruments need different amounts of loosening — and different KINDS of loosening; a single global groove shape can't make drums wobble faster than a vocal or give one stem a dirtier noise floor than another.
features.when_to_use: When per-instrument control over humanization is needed and stems exist; reach for Custom groove specifically when one stem needs a different wow/depth/noise-floor character than the rest of the mix.
features.desktop_location: Mix/Master > Analog Feel card > per-stem lanes + Per-Stem Render (Custom toggle per lane)

features.name: Analog Feel
features.short_description: One-click analog character: tick tape drift, fader ride and/or room tone, pick an amount, render once.
features.detailed_description: Renders the characters you tick at the chosen amount in a single pass and loads the result as the loudness-matched A/B B side. With stems, tape drift runs per stem (each with its own seed, so drums and vocals don't wobble in lockstep and no stem's transients are smeared), then the fader ride and room tone run once on the re-summed mix, true-peak capped at -1 dBTP. Reframed on 2026-11-07 from the closed-loop 'targeted humanize': it no longer runs the AI-artifact scanner, has no detector-confidence target and no escalate-until-it-passes loop. Endpoint: POST /humanize/analog_feel.
features.logic_and_math: amount in [0,1]; timing_intensity = amount if tape_drift else 0, level_intensity = amount if fader_ride else 0, noise_intensity = amount if room_tone else 0, passed to the shared _apply_humanize. Stem branch: per-stem timing with seed + crc32(stem) % 1000, sum, then level/noise on the sum, then a true-peak-safe gain. Single pass; seeded for reproducibility.
features.why_it_exists: A fast, musical starting point for making programmed parts feel played, without dialling four shaping sliders. Results are judged by ear in the A/B, because the goal is a better-sounding record, not a different detector score.
features.when_to_use: When a stiff part needs life quickly; with stems when drums and vocals need their drift kept separate.
features.desktop_location: Mix/Master > Analog Feel card > Analog Feel button + Tape drift / Fader ride / Room tone toggles

features.name: Clean Delivery Metadata
features.short_description: Writes a _clean copy without workflow / personal tags; keeps identity, rights and every AI-provenance or disclosure tag.
features.detailed_description: Copies the file beside the source (audio byte-identical) and removes only workflow and personal clutter: comments, encoder / software / 'encoded by' tags, private application data (ID3 PRIV/GEOB), the original file name and file owner. Title, artist, ISRC, copyright, credits, lyrics and artwork stay. Any tag that carries AI-provenance or disclosure information is never removed and is reported back. Reframed on 2026-11-07 from 'Strip Metadata', which deleted every tag. Endpoint: POST /metadata/clean.
features.logic_and_math: Each tag is classified provenance / workflow / keep. Provenance wins: a key naming C2PA, JUMBF, digital source type, content credentials or AI disclosure, or text matching the provenance detector's generator and generic-AI patterns (metadata_tier.match_services / match_generic). Workflow: ID3 COMM/TSSE/TENC/PRIV/GEOB/TOFN/TOWN, TXXX/Vorbis/APE/MP4 freeform keys such as comment, encoder, software, tool, project, path, and the MP4 comment/tool/encoder atoms. Everything else is kept. RIFF INFO/bext chunks are not edited.
features.why_it_exists: Delivered files often carry private notes, project paths and software tags. A deliverable should keep its identity and rights, and provenance / disclosure information must survive.
features.when_to_use: Before sending a master to a client, distributor or collaborator.
features.desktop_location: Mix/Master > Analog Feel card > Clean Metadata

features.name: Targeted Humanize (Closed Loop)
features.short_description: Scans for the specific AI tells that fired, humanizes only the matching mechanisms, and re-scans - escalating until confidence hits a target.
features.detailed_description: Runs the AI-artifact scan, maps each fired tell to the one humanize mechanism that addresses it, renders, then re-scans and raises intensity until artifact confidence reaches the target or the iteration budget is spent. When stems are supplied it humanizes per-stem (drum-grid tells loosen the drum stem, vocal-pitch tells the vocal stem) and re-sums to a peak-safe mix. Tells that humanization cannot address (a hard spectral ceiling, copy-paste section similarity) are reported as unaddressable instead of being silently ignored. Endpoint: POST /humanize/targeted.
features.logic_and_math: Per-tell mapping: uniform_noise_floor->noise, macro_dynamics->level, drum_timing_grid/repeated_hit_variance/vocal_micro_pitch->timing; metadata and spectral_ceiling/section_similarity engage nothing (the last two are surfaced as unaddressable). Only the mapped mechanisms' intensities are set; the rest stay 0 so an unrelated mechanism never touches audio that didn't trigger it. Closed loop: scan -> if confidence <= target or no mechanism engaged, stop; else render, re-scan, multiply intensity by 1.5 (cap 1.0), repeat up to max_iterations. Stem-aware branch routes deep tells to their own stem via a stem->(name, mechanism) table, sums, then applies mix-level noise/level to the sum and normalizes to -0.3 dBFS.
features.why_it_exists: Global humanize at a manual 3-detent intensity over-processes audio for tells that never fired and can't tell whether it worked. Closing the loop against the detector, engaging only the mechanisms whose tells fired, and working per-stem removes just the statistical signatures that were actually present - the minimum intervention that clears the scan.
features.when_to_use: When you want the tool to decide how much humanization a track needs rather than picking an intensity by hand, or when stems exist and different instruments need different loosening.
features.desktop_location: Mix/Master > Humanize card > Targeted (closed-loop) action

features.name: Recreate Sound (MIDI Variation)
features.short_description: Transcribes a stem to MIDI and exports a humanized .mid variation to re-perform in a DAW, with an honest transcription-quality flag.
features.detailed_description: Extracts MIDI from a source stem (polyphonic via the basic-pitch 3.11 sub-venv when installed, else a monophonic librosa.pyin fallback; drums via onset + band classification into GM kick/snare/hat) and writes a varied standard MIDI file with per-note timing, velocity, and probabilistic in-key pitch variation. This is a MIDI-EXPORT feature (give the user a varied part to re-perform), NOT an audio humanizer - to mask AI tells in audio use Targeted Humanize. The result reports its extraction_backend and sets low_quality_extraction on the monophonic fallback so a monophonic reduction of a polyphonic source is never presented as a faithful transcription.
features.logic_and_math: Pitched: pyin F0 (or basic-pitch polyphonic) segmented into notes at semitone changes with per-note pitch-bend; drums: onset detection then low(<150 Hz)/mid/high(>4 kHz) STFT energy vote into kick/snare/hat. Variation: timing offset ~N(0, timing_variance), velocity ~N(0, velocity_variance), and with probability pitch_variation_prob a note moves one diatonic step up or down in the key estimated from the notes themselves (Krumhansl-Kessler profiles over duration x velocity weighted pitch classes); with no detectable key there is no pitch variation. RNG seeded from the file path. The file carries the detected quarter-note tempo (beat-fit BPM; 6/8 converted to its quarter-note session tempo) and the detected time signature, with bar 1 placed on the first detected downbeat - 120 BPM and 4/4 only when detection fails. 480 ticks/beat, drums on channel 10.
features.why_it_exists: Sometimes the fix isn't reprocessing the audio but re-performing the part. A varied MIDI transcription lets a producer re-play a stiff or AI-generated line with a human touch. Its fidelity is bounded by transcription, so the quality flag keeps the output honest rather than overselling a monophonic reduction.
features.when_to_use: When you want to re-perform a part in a DAW rather than DSP-process the existing audio; best on a clean isolated stem.
features.desktop_location: Recreate Sound panel

features.name: Dynamic De-Esser
features.short_description: Program-dependent de-esser keyed on sibilance level relative to the whole vocal.
features.detailed_description: Ducks the sibilance band using its level RELATIVE to the broadband signal, so one setting tracks quiet verses and loud choruses alike.
features.logic_and_math: Detector = band_env / broadband_env (both ~8 ms one-pole followers), gated below -80 dBFS so filtfilt edge transients don't trigger during silence. Gain reduction applied when rel > rel_threshold_db (~-12 dB), ratio-scaled, floored at max_reduction_db. Zero-phase band isolation (sosfiltfilt).
features.why_it_exists: A static threshold set for the chorus misses quiet-verse esses and chews the chorus; a relative detector rides the performance like an engineer would.
features.when_to_use: On vocals with wide level swings where a static de-esser needs constant re-tuning.
features.desktop_location: DSP chain builder / Copilot (effect name: DynamicDeEsser)

features.name: Mix Note Colour System
features.short_description: Severity-coloured recommendations plus green notes for what the mix does right.
features.detailed_description: Colours every recommendation by severity and adds green Strength notes so wins are as visible as problems, with a legend on the Analysis and Mix/Master screens.
features.logic_and_math: severity in analyzers = clamp(100*|measured-threshold|/|threshold|,0,100). Colour: >=66 red (severe), 33-66 amber (moderate), <33 blue (minor). Strength notes carry type=Strength, severity 0 -> green and sorted last; excluded from Mix Balance scoring.
features.why_it_exists: A clean mix used to show an empty list (reads as 'no info'); colours plus earned strengths tell the user what to fix, in what order, and what not to touch.
features.when_to_use: Whenever reading Mix Notes to triage the highest-impact fix.
features.desktop_location: Analysis Dashboard > Mix Notes; Mix/Master status legend

features.name: What Changed (Version Diff)
features.short_description: Per-metric before/after deltas plus resolved/new mix-note diffing between any two versions in the render tree.
features.detailed_description: Compares any two versions from the branch-preserving render tree — not just the session original vs. the current A/B B render — across LUFS, true peak, LRA, crest, width, clipping, and AI-artifact confidence, colouring only where the healthy direction is unambiguous. Below the metric deltas, a Mix Notes section lists which artifact-scan findings were resolved (green) and which are new (amber) between the two versions.
features.logic_and_math: Pure diff over the server-cached quick_stats + artifacts_scan results (no new analysis). Before/after combos are populated from controller_.renderTree() — every render ever applied, on every branch, using the same 'R<n>: <filename>' naming as the Render Tree panel — so a sibling branch's render can be picked as a baseline, not only the currently-synced linear path. Green/red on clipping-count down, true-peak crossing -1 dBTP, and artifact confidence down; taste metrics (LUFS, width) stay neutral with raw deltas. Mix-note diffing reuses the two artifact scans' finding summaries already fetched for the metric diff: a finding present in the before scan but absent from the after scan is Resolved; one only in the after scan is New — a free byproduct of the same two network calls, not a second analysis pass.
features.why_it_exists: Answers 'what did that render actually do?' immediately after any apply, so changes are verified, not assumed — and against any point in the render tree, not only the original, since engineers often want to compare two experiments against each other rather than each against the untouched source.
features.when_to_use: After applying any chain/EQ/macro/Humanize render, or when comparing two earlier experiments from different branches of the render tree.
features.desktop_location: Mix/Master > What Changed card

features.name: Intake Progress HUD
features.short_description: Global six-stage analysis progress strip visible on every screen.
features.detailed_description: A slim strip pinned above the content on every screen while an analysis pass runs, showing the six pipeline stages with the current one highlighted and an overall percentage; clicking jumps to the Dashboard.
features.logic_and_math: Stages: Fast, Deep, Sections, Drums, Chords/Ref, Stems. overall% = completed_slots/6. Driven by AppController forwarding onPipelineProgress; auto-hides ~4 s after completion.
features.why_it_exists: Heavy analysis + Demucs can take 15-60 s; without visible progress the app looks frozen or like it might be sending data to the cloud.
features.when_to_use: Automatically, whenever intake analysis is running.
features.desktop_location: Global, above the content area on every screen

features.name: Mix/Master Card Reorder
features.short_description: Drag any Mix/Master right-stack card to reorder it; the order persists.
features.detailed_description: The right-hand card stack (Variant Compare, Streaming Impact, What Changed, Timeline, Signal Rack, X-Ray, Presets, Humanize) can be dragged by its header to a new position. The two compound rows — the EQ Curve card with its Apply button, and the side-by-side Snapshots/Render-Tree pair — stay full members of the same ordered list so other cards can be dragged past or around them, but aren't drag sources themselves since neither has one single header to arm a drag from. A teal insertion line shows where a dragged card will land.
features.logic_and_math: The stack is a data-driven ordered section list (previously a hand-rolled sequence of fixed setBounds calls) so reordering is a list-splice, not a layout rewrite. Each section carries its own layout closure plus a collapsed-height override, so per-card collapse (already-shipped layout memory) and reordering compose without conflicting. Order is serialized as a comma-joined id list and restored on next open the same way per-card collapse state already persists; any id missing from the saved order (e.g. a card added since it was written) is appended in its default position instead of disappearing.
features.why_it_exists: Engineers don't all work the cards in the same sequence — someone doing a mastering pass wants X-Ray and Presets up top, someone chasing an artifact wants What Changed and Humanize together. A fixed stack forced everyone into one workflow.
features.when_to_use: Whenever the default Mix/Master card order doesn't match how you work a session — drag a card's header to move it.
features.desktop_location: Mix/Master screen, right-hand card stack
inputs: Mouse drag on a card header

features.name: Multi-File Intake Queue
features.short_description: Drag-reorderable, per-file-cancellable queue for analyzing several tracks in one intake pass.
features.detailed_description: Session Intake accepts multiple files at once and analyzes them sequentially, showing each file's status (Pending/Analyzing/Done/Failed/Cancelled). Rows can be dragged to reorder the queue before or during analysis, and each row has its own Cancel control. The first file to finish auto-populates the Creative Target panel so Create Session unlocks without waiting for the whole queue.
features.logic_and_math: Each file is analyzed via the job-based API (startAnalysisJob, then polling getAnalysisProgress every 100 ms) instead of one blocking analyze() call per file. Cancel sets a per-path atomic flag checked on every poll tick; a flagged file calls cancelAnalysisJob and breaks out of the poll loop immediately, then the queue moves on to the next file. This replaced an earlier version where Cancel only skipped files that hadn't started yet — clicking Cancel on the file currently being analyzed did nothing until its single blocking HTTP call finished (up to 60 s later).
features.why_it_exists: Batch intake of an EP or album shouldn't require babysitting one file at a time, and a queue without real mid-flight cancellation means a wrong file dropped in can waste a full analysis pass with no way to stop it.
features.when_to_use: Loading more than one track at intake — an EP, an album, or several mix revisions to compare.
features.desktop_location: Session Intake screen, file queue below the drop zone

features.name: Mastering Agent
features.short_description: Iterative render → re-analyze → critique → adjust loop that polishes a chain toward genre targets.
features.detailed_description: Renders the current chain, re-measures LUFS/crest/spectral-centroid against the genre target, picks whichever dimension is furthest out of tolerance, nudges the one chain stage that addresses it (gain, compressor ratio, or a broad shelf), and repeats. Every iteration is checked against the same post-render guardrail used elsewhere (matched-level true-peak/clipping/mono-fold/vocal-presence/artifact regressions) before it can be promoted as a candidate — an iteration that regresses a safety metric stops the loop rather than being scored on numeric closeness alone. The agent never auto-applies a result: it proposes a best-safe candidate and the desktop A/B's it against the source at matched loudness for the user to accept.
features.logic_and_math: Objective score = |lufs_delta|/0.5dB + |crest_delta|/1.5dB + |centroid_delta|/400Hz, plus a safety penalty term (vocal-presence drop / 0.05, artifact-score rise / 0.15, each floored at 0 so an improvement never helps the score beyond neutral). Converges when all three deltas are within tolerance; stops early on a safety regression, a soft-safety warning, or 2 consecutive non-improving iterations. The critique step is a deterministic heuristic (worst-dimension-first), not an LLM call, so the loop always completes without any network dependency — an LLM-backed critique is a documented drop-in replacement, not the current implementation.
features.why_it_exists: Manually chasing a genre-target render by ear across many small adjustments is slow; this automates the repetitive polishing step while keeping every decision traceable (each iteration records its chain, metrics, deltas, and a plain-English critique) and keeping the user as the final approver rather than silently swapping in a render.
features.when_to_use: After an initial mix/master chain is in place and you want to close the remaining gap to a genre's loudness/dynamics/tonal targets without manually re-rendering and re-measuring by hand.
features.desktop_location: Mix / Master screen → Mastering Agent action
inputs: Current processing chain (or none, to start from the source)
Rendered audio at each iteration (via the Python analysis service)

features.name: Fix Check (Did it work?)
features.short_description: After each fix, Khensu re-analyses the new version and says, finding by finding, whether the fix worked.
features.detailed_description: Every time a version is accepted (a fix, an EQ, a master, a chain), Khensu analyses that version in the background and compares it with the original's findings: each one is resolved, improved, unchanged (within 5 severity points), worse or new, with the loudness, true peak, loudness range, crest, tonal tilt, width and correlation deltas behind it. The result shows in the issue queue and the sidebar. Checks are kept per version, so undo and redo show the right one without re-analysing.
features.why_it_exists: A fix that only sounds better because it is louder, or that fixes one thing and breaks another, should be caught. The check is the audit trail for every change.
features.when_to_use: Read it after every fix; press Check again in the issue queue to re-run it.
features.desktop_location: Issues screen header (Current version checked: ...) and each issue's check label; sidebar status

features.name: Start From: Current Version
features.short_description: Renders process the current version, so fixes stack; switch to the original to start over.
features.detailed_description: Every render - a fix, the EQ, a cleanup, a chain, the Mastering Agent, chat, AutoMix, presets, the hosted plugin chain, the vocal editors' mix renders - processes the current version by default, so fixing issue 2 keeps the fix for issue 1 and a master carries the EQ before it. The transport bar's Start from choice switches to the original for a fresh branch. The render tree shows each version as a child of the version it was made from.
features.why_it_exists: Fixes used to replace each other: every render started from the original file.
features.when_to_use: Leave it on Current version while working through the issue queue; choose Original to try a different approach from scratch.
features.desktop_location: Transport bar, right of Undo / Redo (once a version exists)

features.name: Results Gate & Provisional Readings
features.short_description: Findings and grades appear when everything a grade is built from has finished; the fast loudness reading shows at once.
features.detailed_description: While a track is analysed, the result screens show progress instead of findings, so grades never move while you read. The gate waits only for the main analysis (deep pass, sections, drums, reference, chords, measurement trust); the Dashboard's other scans fill in their panels afterwards, and the sidebar says while they run. The fast native pass - integrated loudness, true peak, clipping - shows on the progress card at once, marked provisional. Scan results are kept on disk by the file's content, so reopening a session or restarting the app reads them back instead of scanning again.
features.why_it_exists: Results used to stay hidden until a dozen scans that cannot change a grade had finished - up to minutes for nothing.
features.when_to_use: Automatic on every analysis.
features.desktop_location: Over the result screens while analysing; sidebar analysis status
